mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 5% in the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The S&P 500 tends to show positive forward returns over the next 5 trading days following a CPI release that is lower than the previous month's figure, indicating lower inflationary pressure and potential for monetary easing.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where the CPI is lower than the previous month, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenues and earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) both increase within the last month, it suggests a tightening monetary policy coupled with a weakening labor market, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both increase in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this interaction-driven mechanism remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
